# International Graduates: Coordinated-View Dashboard Prototypes

CS 1710 assignment: two interactive mini-dashboards for the guiding question

> Where do international graduates work, and how does their pay compare with domestic graduates in similar fields?

**All data is synthetic.** Country, field, industry and occupation names are real categories. Every count, salary and relationship is generated by `data/generate_synthetic.js`. See `data/DATA_README.md`.

## Run locally

```sh
cd Dashboard_Prototypes
npm install
npm run dev            # open the printed URL
```

| Route | What it is |
|---|---|
| `/` | Landing page linking both prototypes |
| `/prototype-1` | **Exploration-first.** A large country → field → industry flow diagram, with linked employment bars and a salary dumbbell |
| `/prototype-2` | **Comparison-first.** A large salary dumbbell (sort and gap-unit controls) and employment bars, with a compact linked flow diagram |

Each route loads its own data and has its own selection state, so each works on its own as a shareable URL. `npm run build` builds both routes. `npm run generate-data` regenerates the CSVs, and a fixed seed makes the output identical every time.

## Interactions (both prototypes)

- **Click** a flow node, ribbon, bar or salary row to select it. Click it again to deselect it.
- **Degree level** buttons scope every view (both tables have this column).
- **Industry / Occupation** toggle on the employment chart. Choosing an occupation also selects its industry.
- **Hover** shows tooltips. Every tooltip carries a "Synthetic · illustrative only" tag and names its source table.
- **Reset:** the "Reset all" button, the ✕ on each chip, the `Esc` key, or a click on an empty chart area (which clears selections but keeps the degree level).

## What is recomputed, and what isn't

| Selection | Flow diagram | Employment bars | Salary dumbbell |
|---|---|---|---|
| Degree level | relaid out for that level | recounted | shows only that level's rows |
| Origin | matching share drawn solid | recounted | **salaries unchanged**; Share column recounted; fields with 0 dimmed |
| Field | matching share drawn solid | recounted | that field emphasized |
| Industry / occupation | matching share drawn solid | selected bar emphasized (occupation view lists that industry's occupations) | **salaries unchanged**; Share column recounted; fields with 0 dimmed |

The salary table has only field × degree × group, so it is never filtered by origin, industry or occupation, and medians are never averaged across degree levels. Every percentage states its denominator (the in-scope count) in the caption or tooltip.

## Files

- `src/lib/data.js`: category orders, loading, formatters
- `src/lib/selection.svelte.js`: per-page selection state (`Selection` class)
- `src/lib/FlowDiagram.svelte`: parallel sets, hand-built with D3 so ribbons keep their origin color through all three columns
- `src/lib/EmploymentBars.svelte`, `src/lib/SalaryDumbbell.svelte`: linked charts
- `src/lib/SelectionBar.svelte`, `Tooltip.svelte`, `DataNotice.svelte`, `OriginLegend.svelte`, `usePage.svelte.js`: shared page parts
- `src/routes/prototype-1/`, `src/routes/prototype-2/`: the two layouts

## Deploying

The project uses `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` (like the labs), which detects Vercel, Netlify and similar hosts. For a subpath host such as GitHub Pages, switch to `adapter-static` and set `paths.base`. Data URLs go through `asset()` and links through `resolve()`, so both follow the base path.
